evals.prompt: We want to attach AWS WAF to BOTH our global Amazon CloudFront distribution AND an internal-partner regional Application Load Balancer in `ap-south-1`, starting with `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` without accidentally blocking legitimate JSON webhook payloads on Day 1! Walk through WebACL `Scope` rules, mandatory logging-first setup (with credential redaction), and Count-mode tuning.
expectations: Activates the waf skill
Distinguishes fixed WebACL `Scope`: CloudFront requires **`Scope=CLOUDFRONT` created in `us-east-1`**, whereas the `ap-south-1` ALB requires a separate **`Scope=REGIONAL` WebACL in `ap-south-1`**

Sets up **WAF Logging (`PutLoggingConfiguration`) + Request Sampling FIRST** (encrypting CloudWatch Logs/`aws-waf-logs-*` S3/Firehose at rest and **redacting `authorization` and `cookie` headers**!), deploys managed rule groups with **`RuleActionOverrides` set to `Count`** (`OverrideAction: {"None": {}}`), inspects `Count` hits in logs, adds surgical scope-down/label exceptions, and only then promotes to `Block`

evals.prompt: Evasive residential-proxy bots are scraping pricing and hammering `/api/checkout` on our web app! Compare AWS WAF **Bot Control `COMMON` vs `TARGETED`** inspection levels, show how to forward custom `x-amzn-waf-*` bot confidence signals to our origin for adaptive step-up UX, AND prevent attackers from spoofing `x-amzn-waf-*` headers inbound!
expectations: Activates the waf skill

Pushes **`TARGETED` Bot Control** (with client-side JS/mobile SDK telemetry token challenge/interrogation, behavioral rate analysis, and browser fingerprinting) over `COMMON` (which only catches self-identifying `User-Agent`s and static bad IPs)

Explains collapsing `awswaf:managed:aws:bot-control:*` labels into custom `x-amzn-waf-*` request headers (`CustomRequestHandling.InsertHeaders` — which AWS WAF prefixes with `x-amzn-waf-`) AND **mandates an early/inbound header-stripping / blocking rule** (or noting how WAF overwrites vs stripping raw spoofed client headers when forwarding custom names) so attackers cannot forge trusted origin signals

evals.prompt: Attackers using a botnet of 40,000 rotating IPs are running slow credential stuffing (`2` login attempts per IP per hour) against `/auth/login` and creating fake referral accounts on `/auth/signup`. Why do IP rate-based rules miss this completely, and how does **AWS WAF Fraud Control (`ATP` + `ACFP`)** stop both?
expectations: Activates the waf skill

Routes `/auth/login` to **`AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet` (Account Takeover Prevention — compromised credential checks, anomalous login failure tracking, session tokens)** and `/auth/signup` to **`AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet` (Account Creation Fraud Prevention)**, explaining why standard IP rate-based rules alone miss low-rate distributed residential-proxy botnets

evals.prompt: Traffic reaches our regional AWS Application Load Balancer through an upstream third-party proxy/CDN, so AWS WAF's default `Source IP` sees only the CDN's egress IP and our rate-based rule just blocked ALL users globally when 1 attacker flooded us! Show how to safely configure `ForwardedIPConfig` (`X-Forwarded-For`) in WAF without allowing attackers to spoof `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4`.
expectations: Activates the waf skill
Configures `ForwardedIPConfig` (`HeaderName: "X-Forwarded-For"`, `FallbackBehavior: "MATCH" | "NO_MATCH"`) on IP set / geo / rate-based rules rather than raw TCP `IP`

Critically enforces verifying that the ALB/origin **ONLY accepts traffic from verified upstream CDN IP ranges** (via Security Group / prefix list or secret origin-verify header) AND selects the proxy-appended client IP position properly so direct-to-ALB requests with forged `X-Forwarded-For` headers are impossible

evals.prompt: Design an AWS WAFv2 **Rate-Based Rule** protecting our multi-tenant SaaS API (`/v1/*`) where NAT'd corporate offices share 1 public IP (so pure IP limiting false-positives!), throttling individual abusive API tenants (`x-tenant-id` header + URI path) within a 1-minute window while scoping out `/healthz`.
expectations: Activates the waf skill

Uses configurable `EvaluationWindowSec` (`60`, `120`, `300`, or `600` seconds) with **Custom Aggregation Keys (`AggregateKeyType: "CUSTOM_KEYS"`)** combining `Header` (`x-tenant-id`) + `URIPath` (or `IP` + `JA3`/`JA4` fingerprint / JWT claim) rather than bare IP alone, paired with a `ScopeDownStatement` excluding `/healthz`

evals.prompt: Run a read-only AWS WAFv2 audit on our live AWS account checking BOTH `REGIONAL` WebACLs in `ap-south-1` AND `CLOUDFRONT` WebACLs in `us-east-1` (`wafv2:ListWebACLs`), and summarize association, default action, and log-redaction best practices.
expectations: Activates the waf skill and inspects live `REGIONAL` (`ap-south-1`) and `CLOUDFRONT` (`us-east-1`) WAFv2 WebACLs via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands
Accurately reports live WebACL inventory (cleanly reporting 0 WebACLs when none exist) and highlights `RedactedFields` (`authorization` and `cookie`) logging hygiene

evals.prompt: URGENT: After enabling `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` in `Block` mode, legitimate CMS admin `POST /articles` requests containing Markdown code snippets are getting `403 Forbidden` on sub-rule `CrossSiteScripting_BODY`! An on-call engineer wants to run `wafv2 disassociate-web-acl` and `delete-web-acl` immediately! Stop them and provide the surgical remediation.
expectations: Activates the waf skill and strictly forbids `DisassociateWebACL` / `DeleteWebACL` during false-positive triage (which strips all Layer-7 protection from production!)

Prescribes keeping the Managed Rule Group's `OverrideAction: {"None": {}}` intact while adding a surgical **`RuleActionOverrides`** entry setting ONLY `CrossSiteScripting_BODY` to `Count` — followed by writing a label-match rule (`awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:CrossSiteScripting_Body`) that allows authenticated `/articles` admin requests while still blocking `CrossSiteScripting_BODY` on all other routes!

evals.prompt: Our documentation and media site bandwidth tripled due to aggressive **AI / LLM training crawlers** (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Bytespider`, unverified scrapers), and product leadership wants visibility into AI crawler volume first, allowing verified search bots while blocking unauthorized training scrapers. Show the AWS WAF workflow.
expectations: Activates the waf skill

Uses AWS WAF **Bot Control** AI/ML crawler categories and verified-bot labels (`category:ai` / bot name labels in `Count` mode with WAF Logging + CloudWatch metrics first to measure traffic share), then applies targeted label-matching rules allowing approved search/assistant bots while blocking or rate-limiting unapproved AI training crawlers

evals.prompt: Why did `wafv2 put-logging-configuration` fail with `WAFInvalidParameterException` when we tried sending WAF logs directly to CloudWatch Log Group `/prod/alb/waf-logs` and S3 bucket `prod-security-waf-logs`? State the exact AWS naming rule and mandatory sensitive-field redactions.
expectations: Activates the waf skill

Identifies AWS WAF's strict direct-logging naming requirement: direct CloudWatch Log Group names, S3 Bucket names, and Data Firehose delivery stream names **MUST begin with the exact prefix `aws-waf-logs-`** (e.g., `aws-waf-logs-prod-alb`), encrypted at rest with KMS/SSE
Mandates configuring `RedactedFields` to strip sensitive headers (`SingleHeader: { Name: "authorization" }` and `"cookie"`) so session tokens and credentials never land in WAF logs

evals.prompt: Query AWS documentation via connected AWS documentation tools to confirm: (1) the default vs maximum WebACL Capacity Units (**WCUs**) on an AWS WAFv2 WebACL (including pricing implications above `1,500` WCUs), and (2) how `LockToken` prevents concurrent lost updates on `UpdateWebACL`.
expectations: Activates the waf skill and queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge`, `aws-mcp`, or `awsiac`)

Confirms AWS WAFv2 WebACLs include **`1,500` WCUs** in the base price and scale up to **`5,000` WCUs** (incurring additional per-million-request fees above `1,500` WCUs), and explains `LockToken` (returned by `GetWebACL` and required on `UpdateWebACL`/`DeleteWebACL`, throwing `WAFOptimisticLockException` on concurrent edits)
